messages.subject: problem with bivariate normal!!!
parts:
Hi, all. This is the problem that I was having the other day, I stripped down the model and stripped it down and stripped it down until I came up with the following two examples. I can't figure out what is going on! It's the simplest Gaussian model, it works fine in one dimension but not in two dimensions. I don't know if it's a bug in Stan, or in Nuts, or something stupid I'm doing, or what??? I'm doing 20,000 iterations so I don't think it is a convergence issue.
See you
A

---

In file gaussian1.stan:

parameters {
real b1;
}
model {
b1 ~ normal (0, 1);
}

---

In file gaussian2.stan:

parameters {
real b1;
real b2;
}
model {
b1 ~ normal (0, 1);
b2 ~ normal (0, 1);
}

---

R script:

library ("rstan")
gaussian1 <- stan (file="gaussian1.stan", iter=20000, chains=4)
sims <- extract(gaussian1)$b1
print (mean (sims))
print (var (sims))
gaussian2 <- stan (file="gaussian2.stan", iter=20000, chains=4)
sims <- extract(gaussian2)$b1
print (mean (sims))
print (var (sims))

---

Output in R console [cutting out the deals on the Stan sampling, which showed no problems]:

> sims <- extract(gaussian1)$b1
> print (mean (sims))
[1] 0.006627426
> print (var (sims))
[1] 0.9961059

> sims <- extract(gaussian2)$b1
> print (mean (sims))
[1] -0.004989011
> print (var (sims))
[1] 0.9606021

---

This happens consistently. It started with a more complicated regression model, then I stripped it down. The bivariate normal consistently converges in Stan to have too low a variance. But the univariate is OK. This is what made me worry that there's some sort of Nuts problem. But I have no idea. Maybe it is some implicit constraint happening within Stan? Or something else? I also noticed the problem when b was a vector; I expressed it above as two scalars (b1 and b2) just to make sure that vectorization wasn't the problem.

parts:
This doesn't make any sense -- the only real difference was a tweak in how the average
acceptance probability (and hence step size) was being calculated. But the fact that
increasing the average acceptance probability makes the problem worse goes in the
wrong direction.

The median is correct and the distribution is appropriately symmetric. The only thought
I have is that the integrator might have been diverging past 1.5 sigma, but in that case
increasing the target acceptance probability (and decreasing the step size) would help.
And increasing the dimensionality by one wouldn't have any big effect.

I'll look into it.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] problem with bivariate normal!!! [major bug in 2.0.1]
parts: > It would be nice to know what caused the problem.

The issue in the noted commit was that the left-hand side of the parent tree wasn't being correctly passed
recursively to the sub trees. This caused premature termination but no obvious bias that I could see, although
I did see some effect on the funnel as noted in the commit comments.

> While knowing what went wrong in the past is helpful,
> I think it's more important to include a test so we can catch
> it if we reintroduce the problem somehow.

I think we are all aware of the need to test sampler validity. Once Dan reorganizes the tests (making it much
easier to run only a few at once) I'll add a rudimentary sampler testing framework. Hopefully it will be
extensive enough to quickly add difficult models as we find them.

> I'm not clear on how to report hashes for this because most
> of them are local merges. My log (I'm in the middle of working
> on the new manual) shows:

The hash is correct for the changes, it just may not reflect the history of our flow. Remember that merging
concatenates the history of the two branches.
